work~aesop.where: The Library · Fables and fairy tales
work~aesop.title: Aesop's Fables
work~aesop.body: Eighty-two of the fables credited to Aesop, a storyteller of ancient Greece, in a lively Victorian telling. Foxes, lions, mice and crows get into trouble, and each tale closes on a one-line moral that has often become a saying.
work~aesop.more: Told in the Library: “The Town Mouse and the Country Mouse” · “The Lion and the Mouse” · “The Hare and the Tortoise”.

work~grimm.where: The Library · Fables and fairy tales
work~grimm.title: Grimms' Fairy Tales
work~grimm.body: Sixty-two tales gathered by the Brothers Grimm from storytellers in Germany, including Hansel and Gretel, Rumpelstiltskin and The Elves and the Shoemaker. Clever youngest children, talking animals and hard bargains appear again and again.
work~grimm.more: Told in the Library: “The Elves and the Shoemaker” · “The Frog-Prince” · “Rumpelstiltskin: straw into gold”.
work~grimm.cta: Grimms' Fairy Tales in the Library

work~arabian.where: The Library · Fables and fairy tales
work~arabian.title: The Arabian Nights Entertainments
work~arabian.body: Andrew Lang's selection for young readers of the tales of the Thousand and One Nights, including Aladdin, Ali Baba and Sindbad the Sailor. Scheherazade tells a story every night, always stopping at the most exciting moment.
work~arabian.more: Stories within stories, told by Scheherazade to stay alive: one of the great story collections of the world.
work~arabian.cta: The Arabian Nights Entertainments in the Library

work~bulfinch.where: The Library · Fables and fairy tales
work~bulfinch.title: Bulfinch's Mythology
work~bulfinch.body: Bulfinch retells the myths of Greece and Rome, and the Norse gods, for readers who want to understand what poets mean when they mention Apollo or Pandora. Later parts tell the legends of King Arthur and Charlemagne.
work~bulfinch.more: Told in the Library: “Echo” · “Narcissus at the fountain” · “Arachne challenges Minerva”.

work~alice.title: Alice's Adventures in Wonderland
work~alice.body: Alice follows a White Rabbit down a hole and lands in a world where she keeps changing size and nobody makes sense. She meets the Cheshire Cat, the Mad Hatter and a furious Queen, and argues with all of them.
work~alice.more: Told in the Library: “Down the rabbit-hole” · “The Cheshire Cat”.
work~alice.cta: Alice's Adventures in Wonderland in the Library

work~lookingglass.title: Through the Looking-Glass
work~lookingglass.body: Alice climbs through the mirror over the fireplace into a land laid out like a chessboard. She becomes a pawn who wants to be a queen, and meets Tweedledum and Tweedledee, Humpty Dumpty and the White Knight.
work~lookingglass.more: Told in the Library: “Alice meets Humpty Dumpty”.
work~lookingglass.cta: Through the Looking-Glass in the Library

work~blackbeauty.title: Black Beauty
work~blackbeauty.body: Black Beauty grows up in a green meadow, then passes from owner to owner: kind ones, careless ones and cruel ones. Through his eyes Sewell shows what thoughtless people do to animals that cannot speak for themselves.
work~blackbeauty.more: A horse tells his own life, and changed how people treated horses.

work~treasure.title: Treasure Island
work~treasure.body: Young Jim Hawkins finds a treasure map in a dead pirate's sea-chest and sails with the squire and the doctor to find it. The ship's friendly one-legged cook, Long John Silver, may not be what he seems.
work~treasure.more: Told in the Library: “The old sea-dog at the Admiral Benbow”.

work~heidi.title: Heidi
work~heidi.body: Five-year-old Heidi is sent to live with her gruff grandfather high in the Swiss Alps, where she runs with Peter the goatherd. Taken away to a city house to keep a sick girl company, she pines for the mountains.
work~heidi.more: Told in the Library: “The mountains on fire”.

work~littlewomen.title: Little Women
work~littlewomen.body: While their father is away at the American Civil War, Meg, Jo, Beth and Amy March grow up with little money and a great deal of spirit. Each sister has her own fault to fight and her own dream.
work~littlewomen.more: Told in the Library: “No presents this Christmas”.

work~anne.title: Anne of Green Gables
work~anne.body: Matthew and Marilla Cuthbert, a brother and sister on Prince Edward Island, ask for an orphan boy to help on the farm. They are sent Anne Shirley instead: red-haired, talkative and full of imagination.
work~anne.more: An orphan girl who talks, imagines and makes a family by being herself.
work~anne.cta: Anne of Green Gables in the Library

work~oz.title: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz
work~oz.body: A cyclone carries Dorothy and her dog Toto from Kansas to the Land of Oz. To get home she follows the yellow brick road with a Scarecrow, a Tin Woodman and a Cowardly Lion, each hoping the Wizard will give them what they lack.
work~oz.cta: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz in the Library

work~velveteen.title: The Velveteen Rabbit
work~velveteen.body: A toy rabbit made of velveteen is given to a boy at Christmas. The wise old Skin Horse tells him that toys become Real when a child loves them for a long time, and the Rabbit longs for it to happen to him.
work~velveteen.more: Told in the Library: “What is REAL?”.
work~velveteen.cta: The Velveteen Rabbit in the Library

work~peterrabbit.title: The Tale of Peter Rabbit
work~peterrabbit.body: Peter Rabbit is told to keep out of Mr. McGregor's garden, but he squeezes under the gate anyway. He eats too many vegetables, is chased by Mr. McGregor, loses his shoes and his jacket, and gets home very tired and rather unwell.
work~peterrabbit.more: Told in the Library: “Peter Rabbit in Mr. McGregor's garden”.
work~peterrabbit.cta: The Tale of Peter Rabbit in the Library

work~happyprince.title: The Happy Prince and Other Tales
work~happyprince.body: A golden statue of a prince sees the suffering of his city and asks a swallow to give away his jewels and gold to the poor. The other tales include The Selfish Giant and The Nightingale and the Rose.
work~happyprince.more: Told in the Library: “The Swallow and the Happy Prince” · “The Selfish Giant”.
work~happyprince.cta: The Happy Prince and Other Tales in the Library

work~lamb-tales.title: Tales from Shakespeare
work~lamb-tales.body: Twenty of Shakespeare's plays told as prose stories, keeping many of his own words. Mary Lamb wrote the comedies and Charles the tragedies. A retelling, so labelled: the plays themselves are the originals.
work~lamb-tales.more: Told in the Library: “Prospero raises a storm”.
work~lamb-tales.cta: Tales from Shakespeare in the Library

work~railway.title: The Railway Children
work~railway.body: When their father is taken away for reasons nobody will explain, Roberta, Peter and Phyllis move with their mother to a cottage near a railway in the country. They wave to the trains, make friends with the station porter and an old gentleman, and save a train from disaster.
work~railway.more: Three children, a cottage by a railway line, and a mystery about their father that they set out to solve.
work~railway.cta: The Railway Children in the Library

work~five-children.title: Five Children and It
work~five-children.body: Digging in a gravel pit, five brothers and sisters find the Psammead, an ancient, bad-tempered sand-fairy who grants one wish a day. Beauty, riches, wings and a castle all turn out to be more trouble than the children expected, and each wish ends at sunset.
work~five-children.more: A grumpy sand-fairy grants wishes, and every wish goes wrong in a new and funny way.
work~five-children.cta: Five Children and It in the Library

work~dragons.title: The Book of Dragons
work~dragons.body: A boy who has just been made king opens a magic book and lets a dragon out of its pages; tiny dragons, then enormous ones, swarm over England until two children find a way to stop them; a boy who loves caves meets a cockatrice. Nesbit mixes real places, silly grown-ups and brave, sensible children.
work~dragons.more: Told in the Library: “The Book of Beasts”.
work~dragons.cta: The Book of Dragons in the Library

work~kidnapped.title: Kidnapped
work~kidnapped.body: After his father dies, young David Balfour goes to his miserly uncle, who has him kidnapped and shipped off to be sold. Shipwrecked in the Highlands, David joins the bold Jacobite Alan Breck, and the two flee across the heather from the redcoats.
work~kidnapped.more: A cheated heir, a shipwreck and a flight across the Scottish Highlands with an outlaw for a friend.

work~prince-pauper.title: The Prince and the Pauper
work~prince-pauper.body: In Tudor London, the poor boy Tom Canty and the young Prince Edward discover that they look exactly alike and change clothes for fun. Then they are separated: Tom must act the king in the palace, while Edward wanders the streets learning how cruel the laws are to the poor.
work~prince-pauper.more: Two boys who look alike swap places, and each learns how the other half lives.
work~prince-pauper.cta: The Prince and the Pauper in the Library

work~robinhood.title: The Merry Adventures of Robin Hood
work~robinhood.body: Robin Hood, outlawed and living in Sherwood Forest, gathers a band of merry men: Little John, Friar Tuck, Will Scarlet and more. They play tricks on the Sheriff of Nottingham, rob the greedy rich, help the poor, and win archery contests in disguise.
work~robinhood.more: The old English ballads of the outlaw of Sherwood, retold as one great book of adventures.
work~robinhood.cta: The Merry Adventures of Robin Hood in the Library

work~carol.title: A Christmas Carol
work~carol.body: Ebenezer Scrooge, a cold and stingy moneylender, is visited on Christmas Eve by the ghost of his partner Jacob Marley and then by three spirits. They show him his past, his present and the future he is heading for.
work~carol.cta: A Christmas Carol in the Library

work~holmes.title: The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
work~holmes.body: Dr. Watson tells twelve cases of his friend Sherlock Holmes, the detective of Baker Street who reads a stranger's life from a shoe, a sleeve or a hat. A red-headed man, a blue jewel in a goose and a speckled band are among the puzzles.
work~holmes.more: Told in the Library: “A battered hat and a Christmas goose”.
work~holmes.cta: The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes in the Library

work~timemachine.title: The Time Machine
work~timemachine.body: A Victorian inventor builds a machine that travels through time and journeys hundreds of thousands of years into the future. He finds humanity split into two strange races, and has to work out what went wrong.
work~timemachine.more: The story that invented the time machine.
work~timemachine.cta: The Time Machine in the Library

work~gulliver.title: Gulliver's Travels
work~gulliver.body: Ship's doctor Lemuel Gulliver is wrecked in Lilliput, where the people are six inches tall, then visits a land of giants and stranger places still. Swift uses each country to poke fun at the way people govern and quarrel.
work~gulliver.more: A traveller's tale that is really a joke on human pride.

work~frankenstein.title: Frankenstein
work~frankenstein.body: Victor Frankenstein, a young scientist, builds a living creature and then runs from it in horror. The creature, abandoned and lonely, learns language and longs for a friend.
work~frankenstein.more: Begun when its author was eighteen, it asks what a maker owes to what it makes.

work~magi.title: The Gift of the Magi
work~magi.body: Della and Jim are young, poor and in love in New York. On Christmas Eve each secretly sells the thing they treasure most to buy the other a present.
work~magi.more: Told in the Library: “Della's one dollar and eighty-seven cents”.
work~magi.cta: The Gift of the Magi in the Library

work~saki.title: Beasts and Super-Beasts
work~saki.body: Thirty-six short stories by Saki, master of the twist. Clever children, tigers, hyenas and pranksters upset polite Edwardian society.
work~saki.more: Told in the Library: “The Open Window”.
work~saki.cta: Beasts and Super-Beasts in the Library

work~homeworld.title: The Home and the World
work~homeworld.body: In Bengal during the Swadeshi movement, Bimala is torn between her gentle husband Nikhil and the fiery nationalist Sandip. The three tell the story in turn.
work~homeworld.more: Tagore's novel of home, nation and conscience, in the English translation he approved.
work~homeworld.cta: The Home and the World in the Library

work~great-expectations.title: Great Expectations
work~great-expectations.body: Pip, an orphan in the Kent marshes, helps an escaped convict, visits the strange Miss Havisham in her stopped-clock house, and loves her proud ward Estella. When money arrives from someone unknown, he leaves for London and forgets his true friends, until he learns where the money came from.
work~great-expectations.more: A poor boy is given a fortune by a secret benefactor and has to learn what really makes a gentleman.

work~two-cities.title: A Tale of Two Cities
work~two-cities.body: Doctor Manette is freed after eighteen years in the Bastille and brought to London. His daughter Lucie marries Charles Darnay, a Frenchman who has given up his noble family, and when the Revolution calls Darnay back to Paris, the careless lawyer Sydney Carton finds a reason to be brave.
work~two-cities.more: London and Paris in the French Revolution, and one of the most famous openings and endings in fiction.
work~two-cities.cta: A Tale of Two Cities in the Library

work~hound.title: The Hound of the Baskervilles
work~hound.body: Sir Charles Baskerville is found dead on Dartmoor, and near his body are the footprints of an enormous hound, just as an old family legend foretold. Holmes sends Dr Watson to guard the young heir, Sir Henry, while he works out whether the hound is a ghost or something worse.
work~hound.more: Sherlock Holmes's most famous case: a family curse, a lonely moor and a gigantic hound.
work~hound.cta: The Hound of the Baskervilles in the Library

work~moonfleet.title: Moonfleet
work~moonfleet.body: In the village of Moonfleet in the 1750s, fifteen-year-old John Trenchard is trapped in a crypt where smugglers hide their kegs, and finds a locket with a clue to the diamond of the wicked Colonel Mohune. Friendship with the smuggler Elzevir Block carries him into danger at sea and in prison.
work~moonfleet.more: Smugglers, a lost diamond and a secret vault in a Dorset village.

work~war-worlds.title: The War of the Worlds
work~war-worlds.body: A cylinder falls on a common in Surrey, and out come Martians in giant three-legged fighting machines that sweep across southern England. A man who lived through it tells how London fell, and how the invaders were beaten in the end by something nobody expected.
work~war-worlds.more: The first great alien-invasion story, and a question about how people treat those weaker than themselves.
work~war-worlds.cta: The War of the Worlds in the Library

work~sonnets.title: Shakespeare's Sonnets
work~sonnets.body: Shakespeare's sonnets were printed in 1609. Many speak to a young man, others to a mysterious "dark lady", and again and again they promise that poetry can outlast time.
work~sonnets.more: Told in the Library: “Sonnet 18: Shall I compare thee to a summer's day?” · “Sonnet 116: Let me not to the marriage of true minds”.

work~blake.title: Songs of Innocence and of Experience
work~blake.body: Blake printed and coloured these poems himself. The Songs of Innocence see the world through a child's trust; the Songs of Experience, added in 1794, see the same world darkened.
work~blake.more: Told in the Library: “The Lamb” · “The Tiger” · “Holy Thursday (Songs of Experience)”.
work~blake.cta: Songs of Innocence and of Experience in the Library

work~wordsworth.title: Poems, in Two Volumes
work~wordsworth.body: Wordsworth's 1807 collection of short poems about nature, memory and ordinary people. This second volume includes the daffodils poem in its first, three-verse form.
work~wordsworth.more: Told in the Library: “I wandered lonely as a Cloud” · “The Solitary Reaper”.
work~wordsworth.cta: Poems, in Two Volumes in the Library

work~keats.title: Poems (1817)
work~keats.body: The first collection by Keats, published when he was twenty-one. It includes On First Looking into Chapman's Homer, about the thrill of discovering a great book.
work~keats.more: Told in the Library: “On the Grasshopper and Cricket” · “On first looking into Chapman's Homer”.

work~mariner.title: The Rime of the Ancient Mariner
work~mariner.body: An old sailor stops a wedding guest to tell how he shot an albatross, and how his ship was cursed: becalmed, haunted and dying of thirst until he learned to love living things.
work~mariner.more: Told in the Library: “Water, water, every where”.
work~mariner.cta: The Rime of the Ancient Mariner in the Library

work~tennyson.title: The Princess
work~tennyson.body: A prince sets out to win a princess who has founded a university for women and shut men out. Between its sections sit some of Tennyson's best-loved songs.
work~tennyson.more: A long poem with famous songs in it, including the lullaby "Sweet and Low".

work~raven.title: The Raven
work~raven.body: On a bleak midnight, a grieving young man hears a tapping at his door. A raven flies in, perches above the door and answers every question with one word.
work~raven.more: A haunting poem of grief whose rhymes and repetitions you can feel in your chest.

work~dickinson.title: Poems: Three Series
work~dickinson.body: Dickinson published almost nothing in her life. After her death her friends Mabel Loomis Todd and Thomas Wentworth Higginson printed these poems in three series (1890, 1891, 1896), tidying her punctuation as they went.
work~dickinson.cta: Poems: Three Series in the Library

work~lear.title: A Book of Nonsense
work~lear.body: More than a hundred limericks about old men, young ladies and their ridiculous troubles, first drawn and written by Lear for the children of the Earl of Derby's family.
work~lear.cta: A Book of Nonsense in the Library

work~garden-verses.title: A Child's Garden of Verses
work~garden-verses.body: Stevenson remembered his own childhood in these short poems: going to bed in summer daylight, a shadow that will not behave, and a swing that lifts you over the wall.
work~garden-verses.more: Told in the Library: “My Shadow” · “The Swing” · “The Land of Counterpane”.
work~garden-verses.cta: A Child's Garden of Verses in the Library

work~gitanjali.title: Gitanjali (Song Offerings)
work~gitanjali.body: Tagore's own English prose versions of his Bengali songs, published in London with an introduction by W. B. Yeats. They speak to God with great tenderness, and number 35 prays for a country where the mind is without fear.
work~gitanjali.more: Told in the Library: “Where the mind is without fear”.

work~crescentmoon.title: The Crescent Moon
work~crescentmoon.body: Prose poems about children and their mothers: where sleep comes from, a child who wants to be a hawker, a little boy who dreams of being a hero on a long journey.
work~crescentmoon.more: Told in the Library: “The Champa Flower”.
work~crescentmoon.cta: The Crescent Moon in the Library

work~naidu.title: The Golden Threshold
work~naidu.body: Naidu's first collection, published in London with an introduction by Arthur Symons. Palanquin-bearers, weavers, fishers, snake-charmers and the street cries of Hyderabad are set to singing rhythms.
work~naidu.cta: The Golden Threshold in the Library

work~kipling-rewards.title: Rewards and Fairies
work~kipling-rewards.body: Two Sussex children, Dan and Una, meet Puck again, and he brings people from England's past to tell them their stories. Poems sit between the tales, among them "If—".
work~kipling-rewards.more: Stories of English history told by Puck, and the first home of the poem "If—".
work~kipling-rewards.cta: Rewards and Fairies in the Library

work~midsummer.title: A Midsummer Night's Dream
work~midsummer.body: Four young lovers run into a wood outside Athens where the fairy king Oberon and his servant Puck are making mischief. A love potion goes to the wrong eyes, and a weaver called Bottom is given a donkey's head.
work~midsummer.more: Told in the Library: “Puck's goodnight” · “Bottom wants every part (Act 1, Scene 2)” · “Titania wakes (Act 3, Scene 1)”.
work~midsummer.cta: A Midsummer Night's Dream in the Library

work~macbeth.title: Macbeth
work~macbeth.body: Three witches tell the Scottish soldier Macbeth that he will be king. Urged on by Lady Macbeth, he murders King Duncan to make it come true, and then has to kill again and again to stay on the throne, while guilt eats at them both.
work~macbeth.more: Told in the Library: “All hail, Macbeth! (Act 1, Scene 3)”.

work~caesar.title: Julius Caesar
work~caesar.body: Afraid that Julius Caesar will make himself king, Brutus and Cassius lead a plot to kill him in the Senate. At the funeral, Mark Antony turns the crowd against the plotters with a speech, and Rome falls into civil war.
work~caesar.more: Told in the Library: “Friends, Romans, countrymen (Act 3, Scene 2)”.

work~gettysburg.title: The Gettysburg Address
work~gettysburg.body: Lincoln spoke at the dedication of a cemetery for soldiers killed at the Battle of Gettysburg during the American Civil War. He asked the living to finish the work of the dead, so that government by the people would survive.
work~gettysburg.more: Told in the Library: “The Gettysburg Address”.
work~gettysburg.cta: The Gettysburg Address in the Library

work~essays-bacon.title: Essays
work~essays-bacon.body: Bacon's short essays give advice on studies, friendship, travel, anger and much more, in sentences built to be remembered. This is the enlarged 1625 edition.

work~walden.title: Walden
work~walden.body: Thoreau built a cabin by Walden Pond in Massachusetts and lived there for two years, growing beans, watching the seasons and thinking about what a person really needs.
work~walden.more: Told in the Library: “Why I went to the woods”.

work~odyssey.title: The Odyssey
work~odyssey.body: After the Trojan War, Odysseus sets sail for his island home of Ithaca, but the sea god is against him. He escapes the one-eyed giant Polyphemus, the witch Circe and the singing Sirens, while at home his wife Penelope and son Telemachus hold off the suitors who want his throne.
work~odyssey.more: The first great adventure story in European literature: a clever hero's ten-year voyage home.

work~king-arthur.title: The Story of King Arthur and His Knights
work~king-arthur.body: Young Arthur pulls a sword from a stone and becomes king of Britain. He wins the sword Excalibur from the Lady of the Lake, marries Guinevere and gathers the best knights in the land around his Round Table.
work~king-arthur.more: The sword in the stone, the Round Table and the knights' quests, told for young readers.
work~king-arthur.cta: The Story of King Arthur and His Knights in the Library

work~hans-brinker.title: Hans Brinker, or The Silver Skates
work~hans-brinker.body: In Holland, Hans and Gretel Brinker skate on home-made wooden skates and dream of winning the silver skates in a great race on the canal. Their father has been ill for ten years, and Hans sets out to find the famous doctor who might cure him.
work~hans-brinker.more: A poor Dutch boy and his sister skate for a prize, while their real hope is to help their sick father.
work~hans-brinker.cta: Hans Brinker, or The Silver Skates in the Library

work~little-princess.title: A Little Princess
work~little-princess.body: Sara Crewe arrives at a London boarding school as its richest pupil. When her father dies and his fortune seems lost, the cruel headmistress sends her to a cold attic as a servant, but Sara keeps her imagination and her kindness, and help comes from next door.
work~little-princess.more: A rich girl loses everything and stays kind, by pretending she is a princess inside.
work~little-princess.cta: A Little Princess in the Library

work~jekyll.title: Strange Case of Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde
work~jekyll.body: The London lawyer Mr Utterson is puzzled that his friend Dr Jekyll has left everything to a violent man called Edward Hyde. As Hyde's crimes grow worse, Utterson uncovers what Jekyll has done with a potion of his own making.
work~jekyll.more: A respected doctor and a brutal stranger turn out to be one man: a short novel about the good and evil in everyone.
work~jekyll.cta: Strange Case of Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde in the Library

work~swiss-family.title: The Swiss Family Robinson
work~swiss-family.body: A Swiss pastor, his wife and their four sons are wrecked on an unknown island on the way to a new colony. With what they save from the ship and what they find around them, they build a treehouse home, farm, explore and learn about nature.
work~swiss-family.more: A shipwrecked family builds a whole new life on a desert island, with a house in a tree.
work~swiss-family.cta: The Swiss Family Robinson in the Library

work~panchatantra.where: The Library · Fables and fairy tales
work~panchatantra.title: The Panchatantra
work~panchatantra.body: A wise teacher promises a king to make his three foolish sons wise in six months, using stories. Jackals, crows, monkeys and lions trick and help one another, in tales within tales, each with a lesson about friendship and good judgement.
work~panchatantra.more: Ancient Indian animal fables told to teach princes good sense. Bizzing India tells these stories; we link to its telling.

work~ramayana.title: The Ramayana, condensed into English verse
work~ramayana.body: Dutt retold the great Sanskrit epic in English verse for readers who could not read the original: Prince Rama's exile to the forest with Sita and Lakshmana, Sita's capture by Ravana, and Rama's journey to Lanka to bring her home.
work~ramayana.more: An early English verse telling of the epic of Rama by an Indian scholar. Bizzing India tells the Ramayana; we link to its telling.
work~ramayana.cta: The Ramayana, condensed into English verse in the Library

work~mahabharata.title: The Mahabharata, condensed into English verse
work~mahabharata.body: Dutt chose the central story of the Sanskrit epic and set it in English verse: the rivalry of two families of cousins, the game of dice, the long exile, and the great battle at Kurukshetra.
work~mahabharata.more: An early English verse telling of the great epic of the Pandavas and Kauravas. Bizzing India tells the Mahabharata; we link to its telling.
work~mahabharata.cta: The Mahabharata, condensed into English verse in the Library

work~toru-dutt.title: Ancient Ballads and Legends of Hindustan
work~toru-dutt.body: Toru Dutt retold Indian legends such as Savitri and Prahlad in English ballads, and wrote of her family's garden in Calcutta. The book was published after her early death, and a poem about the casuarina tree of her childhood is still read in Indian schools.
work~toru-dutt.more: Poems by one of the first Indian poets in English, who died at twenty-one; it includes "Our Casuarina Tree".
work~toru-dutt.cta: Ancient Ballads and Legends of Hindustan in the Library

work~charlottes-web.title: Charlotte's Web
work~charlottes-web.body: A girl called Fern saves a runt piglet, Wilbur, who is later sold to her uncle's farm. When Wilbur learns he is to be killed, a clever grey spider named Charlotte sets out to save him.
work~charlottes-web.more: A story about friendship and loss that many children meet as their first great book.

work~hobbit.title: The Hobbit
work~hobbit.body: Bilbo Baggins, a comfortable hobbit, is hurried out of his home by the wizard Gandalf and thirteen dwarves to help win back their treasure from the dragon Smaug. On the way he finds a magic ring and more courage than he knew he had.
work~hobbit.more: The adventure that opened the door to modern fantasy.

work~matilda.title: Matilda
work~matilda.body: Matilda Wormwood reads everything in the library by the age of five, though her parents think books are a waste of time. At school she meets the kind Miss Honey and the terrifying headmistress Miss Trunchbull, and discovers an unusual power.
work~matilda.more: A girl who loves books takes on the grown-ups who bully her.

work~room-on-roof.title: The Room on the Roof
work~room-on-roof.body: Rusty, an Anglo-Indian boy living with a strict guardian in Dehra, runs away to live among the Indian friends his guardian forbids. He finds a room on a roof, a job and a new idea of who he is.
work~room-on-roof.more: Written when its author was seventeen: a boy runs away from a strict home into friendship in Dehra.
work~room-on-roof.cta: The Room on the Roof in the Library

work~swami-friends.title: Swami and Friends
work~swami-friends.body: Ten-year-old Swaminathan lives in the town of Malgudi, dreads his schoolmasters, and lives for his friends and their cricket club. A small rebellion at school turns into a big adventure.
work~swami-friends.more: The first Malgudi book: school, cricket and friendship in a small South Indian town.
work~swami-friends.cta: Swami and Friends in the Library

work~pooh.title: Winnie-the-Pooh
work~pooh.body: Christopher Robin's toy bear Pooh and his friends Piglet, Eeyore, Owl, Rabbit and Kanga have small, funny adventures in the forest: hunting a Woozle, visiting Rabbit and getting stuck, and looking for the North Pole.
work~pooh.more: A bear of very little brain and his friends in the Hundred Acre Wood.

work~frost-stopping.title: Stopping by Woods on a Snowy Evening
work~frost-stopping.body: A traveller stops his horse at dusk to watch snow fill a wood. The horse is puzzled, the woods are lovely, but he has promises to keep and far to go.
work~frost-stopping.more: A short poem about a quiet moment in the snow, and the pull of duty.
work~frost-stopping.cta: Stopping by Woods on a Snowy Evening in the Library

work~phantom-tollbooth.title: The Phantom Tollbooth
work~phantom-tollbooth.body: Milo is bored with everything until a tollbooth appears in his room. Driving through it with a watchdog called Tock, he reaches the Lands Beyond, where the kingdoms of words and numbers have quarrelled.
work~phantom-tollbooth.more: A bored boy drives into a land made of words and numbers.
work~phantom-tollbooth.cta: The Phantom Tollbooth in the Library

work~ballet-shoes.title: Ballet Shoes
work~ballet-shoes.body: Pauline, Petrova and Posy Fossil are collected as babies by a travelling great-uncle and raised in London. With money short, they train at a stage school, and each finds out what she is really meant to do.
work~ballet-shoes.more: Three adopted sisters, three different dreams, and the work it takes to reach them.

work~i-have-a-dream.title: I Have a Dream
work~i-have-a-dream.body: On 28 August 1963, at the Lincoln Memorial in Washington, King spoke to a vast crowd at the March on Washington for Jobs and Freedom. He described the injustice Black Americans still faced a century after the end of slavery, and a future of equality.
work~i-have-a-dream.more: The speech that gave the American civil rights movement its most famous words.
work~i-have-a-dream.cta: I Have a Dream in the Library

work~malala-un.title: Speech to the United Nations Youth Assembly
work~malala-un.body: On 12 July 2013, her sixteenth birthday, Malala Yousafzai spoke at the United Nations in New York, nine months after she was shot for campaigning for girls' education in Pakistan. She asked world leaders to give every child a school, a book and a teacher.
work~malala-un.more: A sixteen-year-old speaks for every child's right to go to school.
work~malala-un.cta: Speech to the United Nations Youth Assembly in the Library

work~harry-potter.title: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone
work~harry-potter.body: On his eleventh birthday Harry Potter, who lives in a cupboard under his aunt and uncle's stairs, learns that he is a wizard. At Hogwarts School he makes two true friends, Ron and Hermione, and discovers why a dark wizard once tried to kill him.
work~harry-potter.more: The book that made a generation of children into readers.
work~harry-potter.cta: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone in the Library

work~wonder.title: Wonder
work~wonder.body: August Pullman was born with a facial difference and has been taught at home. At ten he starts middle school, and the story is told by Auggie, his sister and his classmates in turn, as friendships are tested and made.
work~wonder.more: A boy with a face unlike anyone else's starts school for the first time, and everyone around him has to choose kindness.

work~gruffalo.title: The Gruffalo
work~gruffalo.body: A mouse walking through the deep dark wood keeps the fox, the owl and the snake away by inventing a monster called the Gruffalo, until the Gruffalo turns out to be real and the mouse has to think again.
work~gruffalo.more: A rhyming picture book in which a small mouse outwits every creature in the wood.

work~malgudi-days.title: Malgudi Days
work~malgudi-days.body: An astrologer, a postman, a seller of snacks, a boy who finds a tiger and dozens more live in Narayan's town of Malgudi. Each story is short and gentle, and often ends with a twist that shows people as they really are.
work~malgudi-days.more: Short stories of the people of an imaginary South Indian town, funny and sad by turns.

work~percy-jackson.title: Percy Jackson and the Lightning Thief
work~percy-jackson.body: Twelve-year-old Percy, who has dyslexia and ADHD and keeps getting into trouble at school, learns that his father is Poseidon. Accused of stealing Zeus's lightning bolt, he sets off across the United States with two friends to find the real thief.
work~percy-jackson.more: The Greek myths come to modern America, through a boy who finds out he is the son of a god.
work~percy-jackson.cta: Percy Jackson and the Lightning Thief in the Library

work~premchand-idgah.title: Idgah
work~premchand-idgah.body: Hamid, a small orphan who lives with his grandmother Amina, goes to the Eid fair with three paise. His friends spend on sweets and toys, but Hamid buys a pair of tongs so that his grandmother will not burn her fingers at the stove.
work~premchand-idgah.more: A short story, written in Hindi, about a poor boy at the Eid fair who buys a gift for his grandmother instead of a toy.

work~wonderbook.where: The Library · Fables and fairy tales
work~wonderbook.title: A Wonder-Book for Girls and Boys
work~wonderbook.body: A college student called Eustace Bright tells six Greek myths to a crowd of children at a country house: Perseus and the Gorgon, King Midas and the Golden Touch, Pandora and the box, Hercules and the golden apples, the miraculous pitcher, and Bellerophon and the winged horse. Between the stories the children argue about them.
work~wonderbook.more: Told in the Library: “The Golden Touch” · “Pandora opens the box” · “Hercules and Atlas”.
work~wonderbook.cta: A Wonder-Book for Girls and Boys in the Library

work~tanglewood.where: The Library · Fables and fairy tales
work~tanglewood.title: Tanglewood Tales
work~tanglewood.body: Six more myths, told the way Hawthorne told the first six: Theseus and the Minotaur, the Pygmies, Cadmus and the dragon's teeth, Circe's palace, Proserpina and the pomegranate seeds, and Jason and the Golden Fleece. The stories are long, gentle and full of asides to the reader.
work~tanglewood.more: Told in the Library: “Theseus in the labyrinth” · “Mother Ceres and the barren earth”.

work~faraday-candle.title: The Chemical History of a Candle
work~faraday-candle.body: Michael Faraday gave these six lectures to young people at the Royal Institution in London over Christmas 1860–61. With candles and simple experiments he shows how a flame works, what a candle turns into as it burns, and how our breathing is like a candle burning inside us.
work~faraday-candle.more: Told in the Library: “What candles are made of” · “Why a candle makes a cup”.
work~faraday-candle.cta: The Chemical History of a Candle in the Library

work~fabre-spider.title: The Life of the Spider
work~fabre-spider.body: Jean-Henri Fabre spent his long life watching insects and spiders near his home in the south of France. In these chapters he watches spiders dig burrows, build their webs, hunt and care for their young, and he writes about them like a storyteller. The English translation came out in 1912.
work~fabre-spider.source: J. Henri Fabre, translated by Alexander Teixeira de Mattos, 1912
work~fabre-spider.more: Told in the Library: “The Spider has a bad name”.
work~fabre-spider.cta: The Life of the Spider in the Library

hw~mastiffs.body: an old breed of powerful deep-chested smooth-coated dog used chiefly as a watchdog and guard dog

hw~scamper.title: scamper
hw~scamper.body: rushing about hastily in an undignified way

hw~plight.title: plight
hw~plight.body: a condition or situation especially an unfavorable one

hw~gnawed.title: gnawed

hw~waggon.title: waggon
hw~waggon.body: any of various kinds of wheeled vehicles drawn by an animal or a tractor

hw~tickled.body: touch (a body part) lightly so as to excite the surface nerves and cause uneasiness, laughter, or spasmodic movements

hw~equinoxes.title: equinoxes
hw~equinoxes.body: either of two times of the year when the sun crosses the plane of the earth's equator and day and night are of equal length

hw~notion.title: notion
hw~notion.body: a vague idea in which some confidence is placed

hw~arrant.title: arrant
hw~arrant.body: complete and utter, usually said of something bad

hw~buttercup.title: buttercup
hw~buttercup.body: any of various plants of the genus Ranunculus

hw~cattle.title: cattle
hw~cattle.body: domesticated bovine animals as a group regardless of sex or age

hw~mead.title: mead
hw~mead.body: a sweet drink made by fermenting honey with water.

hw~vales.title: vales
hw~vales.body: a long depression in the surface of the land that usually contains a river

hw~meek.title: meek
hw~meek.body: humble in spirit or manner; suggesting retiring mildness or even cowed submissiveness

hw~purchased.title: purchased
hw~purchased.body: obtain by purchase; acquire by means of a financial transaction

hw~seldom.title: seldom
hw~seldom.body: Rarely; only on a few occasions, not very often.

hw~adorned.title: adorned
hw~adorned.body: make more attractive by adding ornament, colour, etc.

hw~challenge.title: challenge
hw~challenge.body: a task or situation that tests someone's abilities; something demanding

hw~contempt.title: contempt
hw~contempt.body: lack of respect accompanied by a feeling of intense dislike

hw~plodded.title: plodded
hw~plodded.body: walk heavily and firmly, as when weary, or through mud

hw~mischief.title: mischief
hw~mischief.body: reckless or malicious behavior that causes discomfort or annoyance in others

hw~exert.title: exert
hw~exert.body: To put something, such as strength, effort, or influence, to active use; to apply force or pressure in order to accomplish a goal.

hw~petals.title: petals
